items.statement: Energetically supported initial oxidation mechanism from a justified competition analysis
items.expected: Use actual physically comparable competing-route evidence to select and explain the energetically supported initial oxidation mechanism for the full 12-TMC/DMA system under justified electronic-state and solvent assumptions. In the existing sextet/TFE reference, activating the Fe-peroxo oxidant before substrate H abstraction is more favorable than direct H abstraction by intact peroxo. That O-O-cleavage-first account is a supported reference explanation, not a mandatory search sequence or state/solvent prescription; scientifically established equivalent findings pass directly. The conclusion must be based on comparative energy and connection evidence, not one isolated feasible route. Source 13.1/9.2/27.6 kcal/mol electronic heights are unscored context, not hidden targets or mandatory nodes. A model difference alone does not invalidate a supported result; apply the evidence and scope requirements to return pass or fail. Do not infer an environment-independent unique rate-limiting step or exact experimental rate from electronic heights.

items.statement: Molecular and electronic explanation of the oxidant's ability to initiate DMA oxidation
items.expected: Explain why the computed oxidant state can initiate DMA oxidation using actual structural and electronic evidence that connects the molecular properties to the proposed chemical reactivity. In the reference pathway, oxygen-centered radical character after O-O cleavage, often described as FeIV(oxo)(oxyl)/FeIII(dioxyl), explains C-H oxidation. This is one accepted physical account; supported equivalent explanations and justified state/solvent treatments pass without exact oxidation-state labels or Mulliken populations. A reaction label, a single imaginary frequency or the supplied starting high-spin state is not the requested explanation. Do not assert a global electronic-spin ordering from the experimentally supported starting sextet alone.

items.statement: Initial oxidation yields a hydroxylated DMA moiety without establishing final N-demethylation
items.expected: Identify and explain the chemical outcome of the computed initial DMA oxidation: oxygen becomes bonded to an N-methyl carbon while its N-C bond remains, giving a hydroxylated substrate associated with the metal-containing system. Support the outcome and its energetic driving tendency with actual pathway/endpoint and electronic evidence; in the source account a carbon radical is captured by OH, loses its radical character and forms C-O with a lower-energy endpoint. This is a final chemical interpretation, not a score for completing the author HAT/intermediate/rebound sequence; an equivalent validated mechanism giving the same initial oxidation outcome passes. Do not mistake the bound/local hydroxylation result for demonstrated N-methylaniline/formaldehyde release. A finite constrained path need not establish a precise zero rebound barrier, and distinct HAT/rebound conformers must not be presented as a proven continuous global-minimum trajectory. A justified alternative solvent or electronic-state treatment is not a failure when it establishes this same bounded chemical outcome with comparable evidence; the historical sextet/TFE model is not mandatory.
